label: copy phase: input w being followed by w (or l), mid-sequence
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only on steps where the input is the fed-back token w (100% of activations). About 80% of the mass falls on steps where the output is also w (an original w w pair) and about 19% where it is l (an original w l pair). It is concentrated at recall_idx 3 (84% of mass), i.e. the w w pair sits at original positions 2-3, and it is stronger for longer sequences (none for L<=4). The strongest examples are like y d w l e s e / 1 x w w e e s, where it fires on the copied w at position 2. It never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any input other than w. Precision is low: most w-then-w/l copy steps that fit these positional conditions stay inactive, and which ones fire seems to depend loosely on the token that follows (e, l, w, x and z are enriched) in a way that no simple predicate captures.
